lines.trans: Marina, let's end this dangerous protest.
Let's go home from here right now.
Listen, Samsonov, you wanted to leave town.
This has long not been your city.
We came here to save you, after all.
I will not leave and will not abandon the students.
Brothers, calm down, these are just ordinary students.
They will soon freeze and leave on their own.
We will stand here until the very end.
A very serious fight will soon start here.
We must protect this historical wall.
Then we will stay near you.

meanings.note: organized public event or campaign
unit of ownership in a company

examples.trans: The students organized a peaceful protest action.

examples.text: Марина, давай заканчивать эту опасную акцию.
examples.trans: Marina, let's end this dangerous protest.

meanings.note: colloquial or affectionate address to a peer

examples.text: Братцы, успокойтесь, это же простые студенты.
examples.trans: Brothers, calm down, these are just ordinary students.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to throw; to leave (someone)', paired with 'бросать'.

meanings.en: to leave, to walk out on (someone)

examples.text: Меня жена бросила. Два пальца сломаны.
examples.trans: My wife has left me. Two of my fingers are broken.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
present есть; у меня есть = I have
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: polite (вы) or plural

examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?

meanings.note: adds a reason or an obvious truth

examples.trans: I did tell you, you know!

examples.text: Садись, не бойся. Я ведь сам чуть тебя не отпустил.
examples.trans: Sit down, don't be afraid. I very nearly let you go myself.

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)
meanings.note: case forms

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'town, city' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: + infinitive: давай убирать = let's clean up
casual goodbye

related.gloss: to give (the verb it comes from)

давно.gloss: for a long time; long ago

meanings.note: with present: Я давно здесь = I've been here a long time

examples.trans: You haven't been interested in me for a long time.

examples.text: Вспомнил? Я давно тебя не интересую.
examples.trans: Now you remember? You haven't been interested in me for a long time.

meanings.note: + genitive
+ infinitive; agrees with the subject: должна (f)

examples.text: Жадность, Паша, должна быть умеренная. Комнатной температуры.
examples.trans: Greed, Pasha, should be moderate. Room temperature.

meanings.note: contrast дома = at home

examples.text: А ты иди домой и делай уроки.
examples.trans: And you go home and do your homework.

examples.text: Так, мы идём к слепым. А ты иди домой и делай уроки.
examples.trans: Right, we're going to the blind people. And you go home and do your homework.

meanings.note: physical combat or brawl

examples.trans: A noisy fight broke out on the street.

meanings.note: adds emphasis to the word before it

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: to bring an activity to an end

examples.text: Марина, давай заканчивать эту опасную акцию.
examples.trans: Marina, let's end this dangerous protest.
The craftsmen are already finishing the complex repair.

meanings.en: to get cold, feel chilled; to freeze solid
meanings.note: intransitive; past tense замёрз, замёрзла

examples.trans: Danya, are you cold or what?
Come on, get up, you'll freeze in the snow!

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'щитить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to protect, to defend', paired with 'защищать'.

examples.trans: He will be able to protect me.

examples.text: Я думаю, что у меня есть мужчина. Он сможет меня защитить.
examples.trans: I think that I have a man. He will be able to protect me.

examples.text: Мы должны защитить эту историческую стену.
examples.trans: We must protect this historical wall.

meanings.note: location
emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: + genitive: 'из мэрии' = from the town hall

examples.text: Марина Сергеевна, я уже знаю. Мне звонили из мэрии.
examples.trans: Marina Sergeyevna, I already know. The town hall called me.

meanings.note: about history: историческое наследие = historical heritage
important in history

examples.trans: This is the historic centre of the town.

examples.text: Я ваш советник по историческому наследию. Забыли?
examples.trans: I'm your adviser on historical heritage. Have you forgotten?

meanings.note: the 'е' drops out in the other forms
radio and phone phrase

examples.trans: At the end of the film everyone is happy.

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)
meanings.note: case forms

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

начаться.gloss: to begin, to start, to break out

meanings.en: to begin, to start, to break out (intransitive)
meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'чаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to begin, to start, to break out', paired with 'начинаться'.

examples.trans: The film started at seven sharp.

examples.text: Там начался пожар! Везде пожарные машины и полиция!
examples.trans: A fire started there! Fire engines and police are everywhere!

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
Core Russian pron meaning 'they' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Ты преподавай. А они пусть строят свои торговые центры.
examples.trans: You teach. And let them build their shopping centres.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('dangerous').

examples.trans: This is a very dangerous job.

examples.text: У меня много опасных друзей. А иначе я позвоню ребятам.
examples.trans: I have many dangerous friends. Otherwise I'll call the guys.

meanings.note: ничего не осталось = there's nothing left

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: locative / directional adverb

examples.text: Я выйду отсюда через две недели. Я решу все ваши проблемы.
examples.trans: I'll be out of here in two weeks. I'll solve all your problems.

meanings.note: with verbs: очень люблю
with verbs: очень люблю

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

поехать.gloss: to go (by vehicle), to set off

meanings.en: to go, to set off (by car, bus, train)
meanings.note: Мы поедем = We'll be off

examples.trans: All right, Arkashenka. We'll be off, it's time.

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'ехать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to arrive (by vehicle)', paired with 'приезжать'.

examples.trans: Which car did you come in?

examples.text: Вика, ты на какой машине сегодня приехала?
examples.trans: Vika, which car did you come in today?

meanings.note: простые люди = ordinary people
простые люди = ordinary people

examples.trans: I know the problems of ordinary people.

meanings.note: прямо так = just like that

examples.text: В смысле, Виктор Степанович? Прямо так, да?
examples.trans: What do you mean, Viktor Stepanovich? Just like that?

meanings.note: рядом с + instrumental
adverb of place

examples.trans: A plot next to Grigory Soprykin.
Right nearby, round the corner, there's a cheburek café.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: сам, сама, само, сами

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

meanings.note: forms the superlative: самый главный = the most important

examples.trans: The most important thing is the people.
Do you know the main thing?

meanings.note: 'сейчас буду' = I'll be right there

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: серьёзный человек
серьёзный человек

examples.text: Я приехала к очень серьёзному человеку.
examples.trans: I have come to see a very important man.

examples.text: Я приехала к очень серьёзному человеку. Он меня ждёт.
examples.trans: I have come to see a very important man. He is waiting for me.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'коро'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Так, не шумим. Я скоро вернусь.
examples.trans: Right, no noise. I'll be back soon.

meanings.note: + accusative
the imperative 'слушай' starts a sentence, like 'look, ...'
'Слушаю' = I'm listening

examples.text: Слушай, Самсон, я тут подумал. Твой начальник — такой опытный специалист.
examples.trans: Listen, Samson, I've been thinking. Your boss is such an experienced specialist.

meanings.en: to save, to rescue from danger
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пасать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to save, to rescue', paired with 'спасти'.

examples.text: Все прибежали тебя спасать — и я, и папа!
examples.trans: Everyone came running to save you — both me and Dad!
She is saving you from the hospital!

meanings.note: of a room, building or fortress

examples.trans: The picture is on the wall.

examples.text: Не надо врать. Стену монастыря сносят!
examples.trans: Don't lie. They're pulling down the monastery wall!

meanings.note: the infinitive 'Стоять!' as a police order
the infinitive 'Стоять!' as a police order

examples.text: То есть просто стоять и смотреть?
examples.trans: So we just stand and watch?

examples.trans: The white one? Give me the keys.

examples.trans: I'll be gone for an hour.

examples.trans: Listen, I'm going out for an hour and a half. You stay with Vika, got it?

meanings.note: уже четыре года = for four years now

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.

уйти.gloss: to leave, to go away (on foot)

meanings.en: to calm down, to settle down

Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to calm down', paired with 'успокаиваться'.
+ infinitive or a noun

examples.trans: If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.

linking word: главное — это народ

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: alone: 'я этого не хочу' = I don't want that

examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat.
